thread:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: model=redwood-quant-v2.4.3, pool=canary-east-1, pct=10% :rocket:
incident-bot: Canary health monitor: probe failures detected (healthcheck 5m window) — failing hosts: 3/5 — auto-abort threshold=3 :rotating_light:
sre-oncall-1: paging oncall — elevated 5xx from canary, seeing a spike around 14:07 UTC. Paging now.
jamal: joining — getting the same. Logs show repeated OOMs in inference worker: "CUDA out of memory" then 502 from the proxy.
priya: quick context: we switched quant profile to int8-fast for this canary to improve throughput. This is the first rollout of that profile on the 80GB A100s in east.
maria: product impact? any customer-facing errors yet?
sre-oncall-1: early telemetry: error-rate bump to ~1.8% overall for the region, top endpoints are streaming/generation. No large customers paged yet but some 5xx traces from a couple of paying teams.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3845 — Canary 5xx surge, auto-abort triggered. Handoff to oncall.
nate: recommending immediate kill-switch of the quant flag for canary and rollback to previous model binary. Can toggle flag via: ````
# disable quant flag for canary
redwoodctl flags set quant_profile=default --env=canary-east-1
# abort canary rollout
redwoodctl rollout abort --target=canary-east-1 --reason "quant-int8 OOM spike"
````
priya: I can flip the flag. Doing it now.
priya: ````
> redwoodctl flags set quant_profile=default --env=canary-east-1
Success: flag updated on 5/5 hosts.
> redwoodctl rollout abort --target=canary-east-1 --force
Abort queued, controllers will shift traffic back to stable within ~45s.
````
carla: watching logs. After flag flip, some workers restarted and OOM frequency dropped almost immediately. Error rate trending down from 1.8% -> 0.6% in last 2 minutes.
jamal: looking at kernel traces — the int8-fast path allocs a temporary KV cache that blows past our per-request budget for long contexts. We should add a guard on kv_temp_alloc.
sre-oncall-1: notify support and customer success: short blip, some retries will have failed. Maria, can you help draft a blameless note for impacted customers? We should say we aborted the canary, rollback in progress, and no data loss.
maria: on it. Draft: "We briefly observed elevated 5xx errors for a subset of requests in US-East during an experimental rollout of a quantized model. The canary was automatically aborted and traffic routed to the previous model. We're investigating and will follow up with root cause and any mitigation steps." Thoughts?
nate: good. Add estimated window: 14:07–14:12 UTC and mention which endpoints were affected (generation streaming).
maria: done, sending to support channels now.
incident-bot: Update INC-2026-3845: abort confirmed, rollback complete at 14:11:32 UTC.
priya: we should also add a short-term gating rule: do not run int8-fast profile on this hardware for contexts > 2048 tokens until backfilled guard is in. I'll open a PR for the runtime guard and a canary test for long contexts.
jamal: for postmortem: include perf regression tests, add a Canary smoke that runs a 4096-token generation against quant profile in staging.
sre-oncall-1: any customer escalations?
support (carla): got two small tickets from customers who saw transient errors; both cleared after retries. No SLA credits requested so far.
incident-bot: Severity: P2 — customer impact limited, auto-abort prevented wider rollout. Root cause: quantized path memory allocation unchecked for long contexts on this hardware.
priya: follow-up actions: 1) PR for kv_temp_alloc guard (owner: priya) 2) Canary staging test for >2048 tokens (owner: jamal) 3) Add quant-profile gating rule for hardware types (owner: nate) 4) Postmortem in /docs/incidents within 48h (owner: sre-oncall-1).
maria: I've posted the customer communication in #support-updates and pinged the small teams impacted.
sre-oncall-1: handing off to next oncall for monitoring window — please watch for any regressions for the next 2 hours. Handoff: I'm off at 14:30 UTC.
next-oncall: ack — will monitor and escalate if error-rate >0.5% sustained.
carla: closing loop with support: will reopen if customers request more.
jamal: logging note: saved a trace bundle at s3://redwood-incidents/3845001234/traces.tar.gz for postmortem.
priya: thanks everyone. We'll track remediation in the canary-failures epic and follow up with a short blameless postmortem. :white_check_mark:
notes: Canary auto-abort due to OOM spike caused by int8-fast quant profile on long-context workloads; immediate mitigation via flag flip and abort; limited customer impact; remediation tasks assigned.
